A **planfile** is a plan the engine keeps after the convergence that made it has ended, for a later
convergence to apply exactly as it was made. It is how a plan is reviewed and approved in one
place and applied in another — a second server, a second session, a second set of credentials —
the way `tofu plan -out` and `tofu apply <planfile>` split a run, except that nothing is written
to disk: the planfile lives in the engine, named by the planned round and the digest of its
document.

## Making one

Add `plan_only: true` to the start verb — `up({ plan_only: true })`, `destroy({ plan_only: true })`,
`refresh`, `import` and `invoke` alike — and plan the round as usual:

```
up({ plan_only: true })                        # awaiting_plan, as every start verb
plan({ convergence_id: "…" })                  # plans the round, then ends: outcome planned
```

The round ends **`planned`** instead of waiting at its approval point: nothing is approved, nothing
is applied, the workspace is free. The result carries:

- `planfile.ref` — the planfile's name (the planned round's id). `apply` and `show` take it.
- `planfile.digest` — the engine's digest of the plan document, `sha256:…` of the bytes
  `show({ planfile })` reads with `show_sensitive`. It is what `apply` names as the approval, and it
  equals `plan.digest`.
- `planfile.expires_at` — when the engine lets it go (the engine's retention, 24 hours by default).
- `plan` — the same summary an approval point hands over (`plan.uri`, the counts, the invocations),
  so the plan is reviewed exactly as a waiting one is.

A plan-only convergence is one round: what it defers stays deferred, and the next plan is another
`plan_only` run. `status({})` and `open` list the planfiles a workspace holds (`planfiles[]`: ref,
kind, digest, counts, expiry, and whether one is being applied).

## Reviewing one

`show({ planfile: "<ref>" })` reads the document (redacted; `show_sensitive: true` for the bytes
the digest hashes). Hand it to your policy tools as you would a waiting plan. The approval rule is
the same: approve yourself only a low-risk plan; consult the user on anything else, and always on a
destroy plan.

## Applying one

```
apply({ workspace_alias: "…", planfile: "<ref>", plan_digest: "<planfile.digest>" })
```

That call **is** the approval, of exactly that plan: the digest you name must be the planfile's,
read from the document you reviewed — any other is refused, and the planfile is left for another
try. It starts a new one-round convergence on the workspace, which must be free (nothing is
superseded for a planfile), and follows it as `apply` follows an approved round: to
`awaiting_actions` for turf actions, to `applying` at the server's deadline, or to its end.
Never with `convergence_id`, `decline` or `action_results`: a planfile names no convergence and
answers no gate.

The engine holds the convergence to the plan, and ends it **`stale`** (`rounds[].stale_reason`
says which pin failed) when anything moved since the plan was made:

- the configuration — a `.tf`, `.tfvars` or lock-file edit, a module source that fetches other bytes;
- the state — any change recorded on the workspace since: another convergence's apply, a `taint`, a
  statefile edited outside Turf;
- the mode or the workspace name — a destroy planfile applied as an `up`, or on another workspace;
- the digest — the plan approved is not the plan sealed.

A stale planfile is left where it was: revert what moved and apply again, or plan anew. A planfile
that **expired**, or was **already applied** (a plan is applied once), fails the call by name:
plan again.

`converged` ends it as any apply does; `exhausted` says the plan deferred work — the next step is a
new plan (`up({ plan_only: true })` again, or `up` without it to run the rounds here).

## Two servers, two credentials

The planfile is what lets a server that can plan but not apply hand its work to one that can
apply but not plan: the first ends every convergence `planned` and reports `planfile.ref` and
`planfile.digest`; a reviewer approves the document; the second opens the same workspace and calls
`apply({ planfile, plan_digest })`. The engine's pins make the hand-off safe — what the reviewer
approved is what applies, or nothing does. The planned round's `approved_by` on the engine's record
names the applying server and its client.

## Tiers

A server runs at a permission tier (`--tier read|plan|apply|full`, env `TURF_TIER`; full is the
default), chosen by whoever launches it: the tools outside the tier are not listed, and the
arguments outside it are refused in words. A credential handed to a server buys that tier's calls
and no other. The server's instructions end with a paragraph naming its tier, so you know which
server you are on.

- **read** — `list`, `status`, `show`, `output`, `state_list`, `provider_search`,
  `provider_describe`, the skills, and `init`, `open`, `close` to bind the workspace a read needs.
  Nothing runs.
- **plan** — the reads, the start verbs, `plan` and `cancel`. Every run it starts is `plan_only`
  whether or not you asked (the result's note says so): `plan` ends it `planned` with a planfile,
  and there is no `apply` here. `cancel` stops a convergence at a gate or planning; one `applying`
  or at `awaiting_actions` is the applier's to stop, and is refused.
- **apply** — the reads, `apply` and `cancel`: `apply({ workspace_alias, planfile, plan_digest })`
  applies a planner's planfile, and `apply({ convergence_id, plan_digest })` approves a plan
  another server left at its approval point. No start verb, no `plan`, no `/up` or `/destroy`.
- **full** — everything, with `taint`, `untaint`, `delete` and `open({ force_unlock })`, which
  every other tier refuses.

The handoff between tiers is the planfile: the planner's `planned` result names it (`planfile.ref`,
`planfile.digest`); the applier opens the workspace and applies it with that digest, as above.
